docs.title: KINO
docs.text:
[K]ino [I]s [NO]t an accronym.*

(kino - the German word for cinema - from the Greek kinema, "movement")

KINO is a Python toolkit to simulate and test the inference of kinematic lensing (KL) - the measurement of weak gravitational shear from the distorted velocity field of an individual disc galaxy. It works across both observing modes used in the KL literature:

  • Integral-field units (IFUs) — resolved 2-D velocity maps / datacubes.
  • Slit / grism spectrographs — 1-D or partially-resolved spectra combined with imaging.

docs.title: The idea
docs.text:
Weak lensing is limited by shape noise: the intrinsic scatter of galaxy ellipticities (σ_ε ≈ 0.26) dwarfs the ~1% shear signal, so conventional cosmic shear must average over huge numbers of galaxies. Kinematic lensing removes this limitation. For a rotationally supported disc, the projected velocity field fixes the galaxy's intrinsic inclination and orientation directly from the resolved kinematics. Lensing distorts the image but not the observed frequency of light, so the mismatch between the shape implied by the kinematics and the observed shape yields the shear for a single galaxy, driving the effective shape noise down to σ_ε ≈ 0.02–0.04.

 intrinsic disc  ──►  apply shear  ──►  instrument model  ──►  mock data
 (image + Vlos)       (g1, g2)          (IFU or slit)          (cube / spectra + image)
        ▲                                                              │
        └──────────────  inference: recover (g1, g2) posterior  ◄──────┘

By simulating galaxies with a known input shear and running the inference, KINO measures the per-galaxy shear precision, quantifies residual shape noise, detects multiplicative/additive biases, and forecasts performance for a given instrument and exposure time — for both IFUs and slit spectrographs, on the same footing.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
In scope: forward modelling of a single sheared disc galaxy (image + line-of-sight velocity field), interchangeable IFU/slit instrument backends, Bayesian shear inference per galaxy, and ensemble forecasting (shape noise, m/c bias, null tests).

Out of scope (for now): real-data reduction pipelines, cluster mass-profile modelling and cosmological likelihoods (KINO stops at the per-galaxy shear estimate), and full radiative transfer (emission lines are modelled parametrically).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
KINO targets Python ≥ 3.10. Clone the repository and install in editable mode:

git clone https://github.com/andrevitorelli/KINO.git
cd KINO
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"

pip install -e "." alone pulls in the core dependencies (NumPy, SciPy, Astropy, GalSim, nautilus-sampler, Matplotlib, PyYAML, h5py). The rest are optional extras, installed as pip install -e ".[extra]" (or combined, e.g. ".[dev,notebooks]"):

Extra What it adds When you need it dev ruff, mypy, pytest, pytest-cov, pre-commit, plus data Developing KINO itself; this is what CI installs. data kinms Generating KinMS-based mock datacubes (kino.io.kinms). sky skycalc-cli Rebuilding the offline ESO SkyCalc sky library (scripts/build_skycalc_library.py) — not needed to use the library, only to regenerate it. notebooks jupyterlab, ipykernel Running the tutorial notebooks in notebooks/. docs mkdocs, mkdocs-material, mkdocstrings[python] Building this documentation site locally.

docs.title: Verify the install
docs.text:
pytest -q

should pass with no failures. If you installed the dev extra:

ruff check . && ruff format --check .

should also pass clean — both run in CI on every push and pull request.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
This is a real, runnable example — every line below was executed against the current API before being written down here. It builds a disc galaxy, shears it, observes it through a real SOAR/SIFS configuration, and forecasts how precisely that shear could be recovered.

import numpy as np
import astropy.units as u
from kino.galaxy import DiscGalaxy
from kino.lensing import apply_shear
from kino.instruments.ifu import IFU
from kino.analysis.fisher import shear_fisher

# 1. intrinsic disc (positions in arcsec, velocities in km/s, angles in degrees)
gal = DiscGalaxy(r_e=0.5, inc=60, pa=35, v_flat=180, z=0.05, sigma0=30.0)

# 2. lens it (reduced shear g = g1 + i*g2)
scene = apply_shear(gal, g1=0.03, g2=-0.01)

# 3. observe it through a real instrument config
ifu = IFU.from_config("kino/config/sifs.yaml")
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
cube = ifu.observe(
    scene,
    line_flux=1e-15 * u.erg / u.s / u.cm**2,
    line_wavelength=0.65628 * u.um,  # rest-frame Halpha
    rng=rng,
)
print(cube.flux.shape, cube.flux_unit)   # (290, 26, 50) electron

# 4. how precisely could this shear be recovered?
result = shear_fisher(
    ifu, gal,
    line_flux=1e-15 * u.erg / u.s / u.cm**2,
    line_wavelength=0.65628 * u.um,
    g=(0.03, -0.01),
)
sigma_g1, sigma_g2 = result.sigma_marginal[:2]
print(f"sigma(g1)={sigma_g1:.3f}  sigma(g2)={sigma_g2:.3f}")

That's the whole forward model end to end: intrinsic galaxy → shear → instrument → mock data, plus the Fisher-matrix shortcut for "how good would this measurement be" without running a full posterior fit.

rng=None instead of a seeded generator returns the noiseless, expected-count cube rather than drawing a noise realisation — useful for inspecting the signal itself before adding noise.

docs.title: MomentMaps(flux: np.ndarray, vlos: np.ndarray, dispersion: np.ndarray, flux_err: np.ndarray | None, vlos_err: np.ndarray | None, dispersion_err: np.ndarray | None, snr: np.ndarray | None, mask: np.ndarray | None, flux_unit: u.UnitBase) dataclass
docs.text:
Per-spaxel flux, Vlos, and velocity-dispersion maps, with uncertainties.

All spatial arrays have shape (n_y, n_x) (see Datacube). flux is in the cube's own flux_unit; vlos and dispersion are in km/s. *_err/snr/mask are None if the input cube had no variance. mask is True where vlos/dispersion are masked (below snr_threshold or otherwise ill-defined) -- flux is never masked.

docs.title: compute_moment_maps(cube: Datacube, *, line_wavelength: u.Quantity | None = None, redshift: float | None = None, lsf_sigma: u.Quantity | None = None, snr_threshold: float = 3.0, subtract_background: bool | np.ndarray = True, check_window: bool = True) -> MomentMaps
docs.text:
Flux/Vlos/dispersion moment maps from cube.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cube Datacube required line_wavelength Quantity(wavelength)

Rest-frame line wavelength -- required if cube.spectral_kind == "wavelength" (ignored, and unnecessary, for "velocity", where cube.spectral_axis already is a velocity).

Spaxels with flux significance below this are masked (vlos, dispersion -> NaN). Only applied if cube.variance is set.

True (default): subtract a per-spaxel background estimated as the median flux across the spectral axis (appropriate for a roughly flat sky/dark pedestal occupying most of the band). This estimator is fragile: if the line fills much more than a third of the spectral window the median sits inside the line's wings, which biases the moments (dispersion above all) and adds noise that the propagated errors do not include -- measured: dispersion_err 4.6x too small when the line filled ~half of a 20-channel window. False: the cube is already background-subtracted. An array (broadcastable to cube.flux, e.g. shape (n_spec, 1, 1)): a known baseline to subtract -- what a forward model has, e.g. :meth:kino.instruments.ifu.IFU.baseline_electrons. Nothing is estimated from the data, so the errors stay calibrated at any window width; this is what IFUMomentLikelihood and the forecast use.

Run the cheap, cube-level too-wide-window diagnostic described in this module's docstring and emit a UserWarning if triggered. Set False to silence it -- e.g. when deliberately exploring a bad window (as notebooks/07_moment_window_width_caveat.ipynb does), or once you've already sized the window with :func:crop_to_line and don't need to be told twice.

Returns:

Type Description MomentMaps Source code in kino/analysis/moments.py 
def compute_moment_maps(
    cube: Datacube,
    *,
    line_wavelength: u.Quantity | None = None,
    redshift: float | None = None,
    lsf_sigma: u.Quantity | None = None,
    snr_threshold: float = 3.0,
    subtract_background: bool | np.ndarray = True,
    check_window: bool = True,
) -> MomentMaps:
    """Flux/Vlos/dispersion moment maps from ``cube``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cube : Datacube
    line_wavelength : Quantity (wavelength), optional
        Rest-frame line wavelength -- required if ``cube.spectral_kind ==
        "wavelength"`` (ignored, and unnecessary, for ``"velocity"``, where
        ``cube.spectral_axis`` already *is* a velocity).
    redshift : float or None, optional
        Overrides ``cube.redshift`` for the wavelength -> velocity
        conversion; ``None`` uses ``cube.redshift``.
    lsf_sigma : Quantity (velocity) or None, optional
        Instrumental broadening to remove from ``dispersion`` in quadrature
        (``sqrt(max(measured**2 - lsf_sigma**2, 0))``). ``None`` skips the
        correction, i.e. ``dispersion`` is the *observed* (instrument +
        intrinsic) width.
    snr_threshold : float, optional
        Spaxels with flux significance below this are masked (``vlos``,
        ``dispersion`` -> NaN). Only applied if ``cube.variance`` is set.
    subtract_background : bool or array_like, optional
        ``True`` (default): subtract a per-spaxel background estimated as the
        median flux across the spectral axis (appropriate for a roughly flat
        sky/dark pedestal occupying most of the band). **This estimator is
        fragile**: if the line fills much more than a third of the spectral
        window the median sits inside the line's wings, which biases the
        moments (``dispersion`` above all) and adds noise that the propagated
        errors do not include -- measured: ``dispersion_err`` 4.6x too small
        when the line filled ~half of a 20-channel window. ``False``: the cube
        is already background-subtracted. An **array** (broadcastable to
        ``cube.flux``, e.g. shape ``(n_spec, 1, 1)``): a *known* baseline to
        subtract -- what a forward model has, e.g.
        :meth:`kino.instruments.ifu.IFU.baseline_electrons`. Nothing is
        estimated from the data, so the errors stay calibrated at any window
        width; this is what ``IFUMomentLikelihood`` and the forecast use.
    check_window : bool, optional
        Run the cheap, cube-level too-wide-window diagnostic described in
        this module's docstring and emit a ``UserWarning`` if triggered.
        Set ``False`` to silence it -- e.g. when deliberately exploring a
        bad window (as `notebooks/07_moment_window_width_caveat.ipynb`
        does), or once you've already sized the window with
        :func:`crop_to_line` and don't need to be told twice.

    Returns
    -------
    MomentMaps
    """
    if check_window:
        fraction, n_eff, n_total = _effective_channel_fraction(cube.flux)
        if fraction < _MIN_EFFECTIVE_CHANNEL_FRACTION:
            warnings.warn(
                f"compute_moment_maps: only {fraction:.1%} of the {n_total} spectral "
                f"channels ({n_eff:.0f} effective) contribute to the stacked spectrum's "
                "flux -- the spectral window may be too wide relative to the line. "
                "dispersion is especially vulnerable to noise from the rest (see this "
                "module's 'window width matters' docstring section). Consider "
                "kino.analysis.moments.crop_to_line() first, or pass check_window=False "
                "to silence this.",
                UserWarning,
                stacklevel=2,
            )

    if cube.spectral_kind == "velocity":
        velocity = cube.spectral_axis.to(u.km / u.s)
    else:
        if line_wavelength is None:
            raise ValueError("line_wavelength is required for a wavelength-kind Datacube")
        z = cube.redshift if redshift is None else redshift
        line_center = line_wavelength * (1.0 + z)
        velocity = (C_LIGHT * (cube.spectral_axis / line_center - 1.0)).to(u.km / u.s)
    v = velocity.to_value(u.km / u.s)[:, np.newaxis, np.newaxis]

    flux_cube = cube.flux
    if isinstance(subtract_background, bool | np.bool_):
        background = np.median(flux_cube, axis=0, keepdims=True) if subtract_background else 0.0
    else:
        background = np.asarray(subtract_background, dtype=float)
        try:
            np.broadcast_shapes(background.shape, flux_cube.shape)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValueError(
                f"known background of shape {background.shape} does not broadcast "
                f"to the cube {flux_cube.shape}"
            ) from exc
    signal = flux_cube - background

    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        flux_map = signal.sum(axis=0)
        vlos_map = (signal * v).sum(axis=0) / flux_map
        dv = v - vlos_map[np.newaxis, :, :]
        sigma2_map = (signal * dv**2).sum(axis=0) / flux_map
    dispersion_map = np.sqrt(np.clip(sigma2_map, 0.0, None))

    if lsf_sigma is not None:
        lsf_kms = lsf_sigma.to_value(u.km / u.s)
        dispersion_map = np.sqrt(np.clip(dispersion_map**2 - lsf_kms**2, 0.0, None))

    flux_err = vlos_err = dispersion_err = snr = mask = None
    if cube.variance is not None:
        var = cube.variance
        var_d = var.sum(axis=0)
        flux_err = np.sqrt(var_d)

        var_n = (v**2 * var).sum(axis=0)
        cov_nd = (v * var).sum(axis=0)
        n_num = (signal * v).sum(axis=0)
        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
            var_vlos = (
                var_n / flux_map**2
                - 2.0 * n_num * cov_nd / flux_map**3
                + n_num**2 * var_d / flux_map**4
            )
        vlos_err = np.sqrt(np.clip(var_vlos, 0.0, None))

        var_m = (dv**4 * var).sum(axis=0)
        cov_md = (dv**2 * var).sum(axis=0)
        m_num = (signal * dv**2).sum(axis=0)
        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
            var_sigma2 = (
                var_m / flux_map**2
                - 2.0 * m_num * cov_md / flux_map**3
                + m_num**2 * var_d / flux_map**4
            )
            var_sigma = np.where(sigma2_map > 0, var_sigma2 / (4.0 * sigma2_map), np.nan)
        dispersion_err = np.sqrt(np.clip(var_sigma, 0.0, None))

        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
            snr = flux_map / flux_err
        mask = ~(snr >= snr_threshold)  # NaN-safe: NaN snr also masks out
        vlos_map = np.where(mask, np.nan, vlos_map)
        dispersion_map = np.where(mask, np.nan, dispersion_map)
        vlos_err = np.where(mask, np.nan, vlos_err)
        dispersion_err = np.where(mask, np.nan, dispersion_err)

    return MomentMaps(
        flux=flux_map,
        vlos=vlos_map,
        dispersion=dispersion_map,
        flux_err=flux_err,
        vlos_err=vlos_err,
        dispersion_err=dispersion_err,
        snr=snr,
        mask=mask,
        flux_unit=cube.flux_unit,
    )

docs.text:
Crop cube's spectral axis to [center - half_width, center + half_width].

The safe-path counterpart to this module's window-width caveat: size half_width to a handful of the line's expected total extent (Doppler range across the field, plus a few line widths of margin) and crop before calling :func:compute_moment_maps, rather than handing it an instrument's full bandpass.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cube Datacube required center Quantity

Line centre, in the same domain as cube.spectral_axis (a wavelength for spectral_kind="wavelength", a velocity for "velocity").

required half_width Quantity

Half-width of the retained window, same domain as center.

required

Returns:

Type Description Datacube

A new Datacube with flux/variance/mask sliced to match the cropped spectral_axis. Assumes cube.spectral_axis is monotonically increasing (true of every cube produced elsewhere in kino).

Source code in kino/analysis/moments.py 
def crop_to_line(cube: Datacube, center: u.Quantity, half_width: u.Quantity) -> Datacube:
    """Crop ``cube``'s spectral axis to ``[center - half_width, center + half_width]``.

    The safe-path counterpart to this module's window-width caveat: size
    ``half_width`` to a handful of the line's expected total extent (Doppler
    range across the field, plus a few line widths of margin) and crop
    before calling :func:`compute_moment_maps`, rather than handing it an
    instrument's full bandpass.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cube : Datacube
    center : Quantity
        Line centre, in the same domain as ``cube.spectral_axis`` (a
        wavelength for ``spectral_kind="wavelength"``, a velocity for
        ``"velocity"``).
    half_width : Quantity
        Half-width of the retained window, same domain as ``center``.

    Returns
    -------
    Datacube
        A new ``Datacube`` with ``flux``/``variance``/``mask`` sliced to
        match the cropped ``spectral_axis``. Assumes ``cube.spectral_axis``
        is monotonically increasing (true of every cube produced elsewhere
        in kino).
    """
    axis = cube.spectral_axis
    lo, hi = center - half_width, center + half_width
    in_window = (axis >= lo) & (axis <= hi)
    if not np.any(in_window):
        raise ValueError(
            f"no channels of cube.spectral_axis (range {axis.min()}-{axis.max()}) "
            f"fall within [{lo}, {hi}]"
        )
    idx = np.flatnonzero(in_window)
    sl = slice(idx[0], idx[-1] + 1)
    return Datacube(
        flux=cube.flux[sl],
        spectral_axis=axis[sl],
        spectral_kind=cube.spectral_kind,
        pixel_scale=cube.pixel_scale,
        redshift=cube.redshift,
        flux_unit=cube.flux_unit,
        variance=cube.variance[sl] if cube.variance is not None else None,
        mask=cube.mask[sl] if cube.mask is not None else None,
        meta=dict(cube.meta),
    )

docs.title: kino.analysis.fisher
docs.text:
Fast shear-precision forecast: a Fisher (Cramer-Rao) bound through the same forward model as the inference likelihoods.

For a galaxy, instrument and exposure this estimates how well (g1, g2) can be measured without running a sampler (a few forward renders instead of thousands), which is what makes it usable for ranking hundreds of targets over a semester.

Two estimators (shear_fisher(..., estimator=...)):

"cube" (default) The bound of :class:kino.inference.likelihood.IFUCubeLikelihood: the model cube mu (expected electrons, sky + dark baseline included) against the data voxel by voxel with var = mu + read^2, F_ij = sum dmu_i dmu_j (1/var + 1/(2 var^2)) + F_prior. Unbiased, and it uses the flux image as well as the kinematics.

"moments" The bound of :class:kino.inference.likelihood.IFUMomentLikelihood: derivatives of the flux-weighted Vlos and dispersion maps weighted by their delta-method errors. Kept for comparison; the moment estimator is noise-biased (below).

Two numbers come out of either: sigma_fixed (only the shear free -- optimistic) and sigma_marginal (nuisance parameters free under priors -- what a real fit faces).

What was validated (see scripts/validate_fisher_mle.py, scripts/validate_fisher_forecast.py and notebooks/data/fisher_validation.json), against maximum-likelihood fits on many noise realisations:

  • cube: maximum-likelihood shear unbiased to ~1e-4 and scatter / Fisher = 0.9-1.3, at every per-spaxel S/N tested (about 5 to 100), including with inclination, PA and v_flat free.
  • moments: scatter / sigma_fixed = 1.01 at a median valid-spaxel S/N of ~23, 1.28 at ~13, 2.2-3.6 at ~7; and a noise bias of ~1 sigma per galaxy that grows toward low S/N and that a stack does not average away. An analytic second-order bias correction fails below S/N ~ 12. median_spaxel_snr and :data:LOW_SNR_WARNING flag the regime.

What the bound is not. It is a statistical Cramer-Rao bound for a perfect model: the data are generated by the same DiscGalaxy family the fit assumes, so the data pin the nuisance parameters (inclination to ~0.1 deg, ...) far below any prior, and the marginal shear precision comes out 1e-3-1e-2 per galaxy for bright targets. Real galaxies have non-circular motions, thickness, warps, an uncertain PSF; that sets a floor the bound ignores. Add one with forecast_ifu(intrinsic_sigma=...) and psf_error=. The bound is also a local, Gaussian approximation: it says nothing about multi-modal posteriors.

:func:shear_fisher_multi generalises the cube estimator to several independent exposures of the same galaxy -- e.g. a slit visited at a few position angles/offsets to cover more of its velocity field, rather than one exposure at a single, possibly misaligned, position angle. Each exposure's own voxel-level Fisher information is summed before the shared nuisance priors are applied once. It does not (yet) support psf_error or the moment estimator.

docs.title: shear_snr(g: tuple[float, float], *, marginal: bool = True) -> float
docs.text:
|g| / sigma along the direction of g (or the mean sigma if g = 0).

Source code in kino/analysis/fisher.py 
def shear_snr(self, g: tuple[float, float], *, marginal: bool = True) -> float:
    """``|g| / sigma`` along the direction of ``g`` (or the mean sigma if ``g = 0``)."""
    cov = self.covariance[:2, :2] if marginal else np.diag(np.square(self.sigma_fixed))
    gv = np.asarray(g, dtype=float)
    norm = float(np.linalg.norm(gv))
    if norm == 0.0:
        return 0.0
    unit = gv / norm
    return norm / float(np.sqrt(unit @ cov @ unit))

docs.text:
Cube-estimator Fisher forecast for several independent exposures of the same galaxy -- e.g. a slit visited at a few different position angles or offsets to cover more of its velocity field, or repeat visits on different nights.

Each exposure's own voxel-level Fisher information (statistically independent noise realisations of the same underlying galaxy/shear) is summed before the shared nuisance priors are applied once, not once per exposure -- the priors describe the one true galaxy, not each observation of it:

F_total = sum_k F_k, then cov = (F_total + prior precision)^-1.

Parameters:

def shear_fisher_multi(
    instruments: list,
    galaxy: DiscGalaxy,
    *,
    line_flux: u.Quantity,
    line_wavelength: u.Quantity,
    g: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0),
    snr_threshold: float = 3.0,
    priors: dict[str, float | None] | None = None,
    steps: dict[str, float] | None = None,
    free: list[str] | None = None,
) -> FisherResult:
    """Cube-estimator Fisher forecast for **several independent exposures of the same
    galaxy** -- e.g. a slit visited at a few different position angles or offsets to
    cover more of its velocity field, or repeat visits on different nights.

    Each exposure's own voxel-level Fisher information (statistically independent noise
    realisations of the *same* underlying galaxy/shear) is summed before the shared
    nuisance priors are applied **once**, not once per exposure -- the priors describe
    the one true galaxy, not each observation of it:

    ``F_total = sum_k F_k``, then ``cov = (F_total + prior precision)^-1``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    instruments : list of IFU or SlitSpectrograph
        Two or more instruments, each with its own exposure time/sky/PSF/slit geometry
        already set (e.g. different ``slit_pa`` values -- split a fixed total time
        budget across them yourself, such as ``exposure_time`` scaled by ``1/len(...)``
        on each). All observe the *same* galaxy and shear point; parameter names/steps
        are shared, so a duck-typing mismatch (mixing an IFU and a SlitSpectrograph) is
        allowed as long as both expose the same ``.observe()``/``.baseline_electrons()``
        API used by :func:`shear_fisher`.
    line_flux, line_wavelength, g, snr_threshold, priors, steps, free
        As in :func:`shear_fisher`.

    Returns
    -------
    FisherResult
        ``n_spaxels`` is summed across exposures; ``median_spaxel_snr``/
        ``peak_spaxel_snr`` are computed over the pooled per-spaxel S/N of every
        exposure's used spaxels; ``line_snr`` combines each exposure's own whole-field
        S/N in quadrature (exact only if every exposure captures the same total flux,
        which need not hold for different slit position angles on an inclined disc --
        treat it as a descriptive summary, not something the covariance depends on).

    Notes
    -----
    Only the cube estimator generalises simply to several exposures (the moment
    estimator's per-exposure noise bias does not combine this way) and ``psf_error``/
    ``psf_bias`` is not supported yet (always NaN) -- extending the joint
    mis-specified-PSF fit to several exposures is future work, not implemented here.
    """
    if not instruments:
        raise ValueError("instruments must be non-empty")
    priors = {**DEFAULT_CUBE_PRIORS, **(priors or {})}
    steps = {**_CUBE_STEPS, **(steps or {})}
    base, names, theta0 = _cube_names_and_theta0(galaxy, g, priors, free)
    n = len(names)

    fisher_total = np.zeros((n, n))
    n_used = 0
    snr_pool: list[np.ndarray] = []
    line_snr_sq = 0.0
    for instrument in instruments:
        fid, cols, baseline, _ = _cube_jacobian(
            instrument, base, names, theta0, line_flux, line_wavelength, steps
        )
        var = np.maximum(fid.variance, _VARIANCE_FLOOR)
        signal = fid.flux - baseline
        spaxel_snr = signal.sum(axis=0) / np.sqrt(var.sum(axis=0))
        used = spaxel_snr >= snr_threshold
        if used.any():
            n_used += int(used.sum())
            snr_pool.append(spaxel_snr[used])
        fisher_total += _cube_information(cols, var)
        line_snr_sq += float(signal.sum() ** 2 / var.sum())

    if n_used == 0:
        raise ValueError("no spaxel passes the flux S/N threshold -- the target is undetectable")
    pooled_snr = np.concatenate(snr_pool)

    cov, fixed, _ = _invert_with_priors(fisher_total, names, theta0, priors)
    return FisherResult(
        sigma_fixed=(float(np.sqrt(fixed[0, 0])), float(np.sqrt(fixed[1, 1]))),
        sigma_marginal=(float(np.sqrt(cov[0, 0])), float(np.sqrt(cov[1, 1]))),
        covariance=cov,
        param_names=names,
        n_spaxels=n_used,
        line_snr=float(np.sqrt(line_snr_sq)),
        peak_spaxel_snr=float(np.max(pooled_snr)),
        median_spaxel_snr=float(np.median(pooled_snr)),
        meta={"estimator": "cube", "n_exposures": len(instruments)},
    )

docs.title: kino.analysis.forecast
docs.text:
Target-level forecast: shear S/N as a function of seeing, for a given night.

forecast_ifu and forecast_slit are the entry points that tie the observing-conditions layer (:mod:kino.observing) to an instrument backend (an :class:~kino.instruments.ifu.IFU or a :class:~kino.instruments.slit.SlitSpectrograph) and the fast Fisher estimate (:mod:kino.analysis.fisher). Given

  • an instrument (its exposure, throughput, detector, PSF machinery),
  • a target: sky position, a :class:~kino.galaxy.DiscGalaxy (geometry and redshift) and the line flux measured from its spectrum (:func:kino.io.spectrum.measure_line_flux),
  • a night, and the shear you expect,

each returns, at times through the night and for each seeing you ask about, the airmass, the sky, the effective seeing, the line S/N and the shear precision and S/N -- all computed with the sky, moon, extinction and seeing appropriate to that moment. Both are thin wrappers around _forecast (below), which does the actual work and is agnostic to which instrument type it was given.

What happens at each (time, seeing) point:

  1. airmass, moon phase/altitude/separation and ecliptic position from the target's track (kino.observing);
  2. a sky spectrum from the offline SkyCalc library, converted to detected electrons per channel on the instrument's own collecting area/throughput (per spaxel for an IFU, per along-slit pixel for a slit);
  3. the line flux dimmed by CTIO atmospheric extinction (include_extinction);
  4. the quoted (500 nm, zenith) seeing converted to the observed wavelength and airmass (Kolmogorov scaling), set as the instrument's seeing PSF;
  5. :func:~kino.analysis.fisher.shear_fisher on the noiseless expected cube (the "cube" estimator works for either instrument; slit losses are inside the model exactly as they are inside a real slit observation).

Assumptions you must be comfortable with (each is also in CLAUDE.md):

  • the instrument's throughput curve is end to end excluding the atmosphere; extinction is applied separately. If your throughput already includes the atmosphere (a standard-star efficiency often does), pass include_extinction=False;
  • the sky model is Paranal's, not the site's; airglow is a whole-night mean;
  • line_flux is the whole galaxy's intrinsic flux (aperture-corrected, magnification neglected -- a few per cent for weak lensing);
  • only the emission line constrains the shear -- no continuum;
  • the spectral window is cropped to window_kms around the line, keeping the instrument's native dispersion, purely so the many renders a forecast needs stay fast -- not a physical limitation (see narrowed_ifu/narrowed_slit);
  • the primary, default forecast (intrinsic_sigma=None) is the idealised statistical bound: real-galaxy floor calibration (non-circular motions, disc thickness, ...) is out of scope for now (2026-09-27 direction) and left as an optional sensitivity comparison, not a required input.

def best_time_index(self, seeing_index: int) -> int | None:
    """Index of the time with the highest shear S/N at one seeing (None if none)."""
    col = self.shear_snr[:, seeing_index]
    if not np.any(np.isfinite(col)):
        return None
    return int(np.nanargmax(col))

def night_summary(self) -> dict:
    """One-line-per-seeing summary: best S/N and when it happens."""
    out = {}
    for j, s in enumerate(self.seeing_ref):

docs.title: kino.analysis.injection
docs.text:
Injection-recovery: apply a known shear, re-observe, and check recovery.

Implements README.md Phase 6's injection-recovery, shape-noise, (m, c) bias, and null-test bullets for the IFU case. Each trial takes an intrinsic :class:~kino.galaxy.DiscGalaxy, applies a known reduced shear (g1, g2) via :func:kino.lensing.apply_shear, observes it through an :class:~kino.instruments.ifu.IFU (one noisy realisation), runs :func:kino.inference.fit_shear, and records recovered vs. input shear. :func:summarize_trials then reduces an ensemble of trials to the calibration numbers a shear measurement needs:

  • multiplicative/additive bias (m, c) from g_rec = (1 + m) g_true + c (needs trials at two or more distinct true shears),
  • residual shape noise sigma_eps, the per-galaxy scatter of g_rec - g_true (the shear-equivalent noise of one galaxy),
  • the mean bias at a single shear (with g_true = 0 this is the null test),
  • the pull (g_rec - g_true) / sigma_post, whose standard deviation should be ~1 if the posteriors' widths are honest.
Design notes
  • The input is a DiscGalaxy, not a Datacube as the original stub sketched: a cube is already an observation and cannot be re-sheared, so injection needs the underlying model. (Known-truth cube recovery, e.g. from kino.io.kinms, is a different check -- fitting an unlensed model to a cube -- and is not what this module does.)
  • Recovered shear is the posterior median. With a finite-width uniform prior and weakly-constraining data the median is pulled toward the prior centre, so a measured m < 0 (shrinkage) is expected at low S/N and is a property of the estimator + prior, not necessarily a forward-model bug -- compare m across S/N before interpreting it.
  • Every trial gets its own child seed (numpy.random.SeedSequence.spawn) for both the noise realisation and the sampler, so a run is fully reproducible from one seed and trials are independent of ensemble order/size. Trials are embarrassingly parallel; callers wanting to parallelise can call :func:recover_shear themselves with their own pool.

def recover_shear(
    galaxy: DiscGalaxy,
    g1: float,
    g2: float,
    *,
    ifu: IFU,
    line_wavelength: u.Quantity,
    line_flux: u.Quantity,
    free_priors: FreePriors | None = None,
    shear_prior_range: float = 0.15,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
    sampler_seed: int | None = None,
    snr_threshold: float = 3.0,
    likelihood: str = "cube",
    n_live: int = 500,
    n_eff: float = 2000,
    keep_posterior: bool = False,
) -> InjectionTrial:
    """Inject ``(g1, g2)`` into ``galaxy``, observe it with ``ifu``, and infer it back.

    Parameters
    ----------
    galaxy : DiscGalaxy
        The intrinsic (unlensed) truth.
    g1, g2 : float
        Injected reduced shear.
    ifu : IFU
        Instrument used both to make the data and (inside the likelihood) to
        forward-model every trial point -- see
        :class:`~kino.inference.likelihood.IFUMomentLikelihood`.
    line_wavelength : Quantity (wavelength)
        Rest-frame line wavelength.
    line_flux : Quantity (energy / time / area)
        Intrinsic (unlensed) line flux, assumed known (fixed in the fit).
    free_priors : dict or callable, optional
        Priors (in :func:`~kino.inference.priors.build_prior`'s format) for
        free parameters *other than* the shear -- e.g. ``{"inc": (30, 80)}``.
        A callable ``f(galaxy) -> dict`` lets priors depend on the galaxy
        (e.g. a Tully-Fisher prior centred on its flux). Every
        ``DiscGalaxy`` field not named here is held fixed at the galaxy's
        true value. Default: shear-only fit.
    shear_prior_range : float, optional
        Uniform prior half-width on both ``g1`` and ``g2``.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, optional
        Drives the data's noise realisation; ``None`` gives noiseless data.
    sampler_seed : int or None, optional
        Seed for ``nautilus``.
    likelihood : {"cube", "moments"}, optional
        ``"cube"`` (default): :class:`~kino.inference.likelihood.IFUCubeLikelihood`, unbiased.
        ``"moments"``: :class:`~kino.inference.likelihood.IFUMomentLikelihood`, whose moment
        estimator has a noise bias at low S/N (see ``CLAUDE.md``).
    snr_threshold, n_live, n_eff : optional
        ``snr_threshold`` is used by the moment likelihood only; the rest are forwarded
        to :func:`~kino.inference.sampler.fit_shear`.
    keep_posterior : bool, optional
        Store the full :class:`~kino.inference.sampler.Posterior` on the trial.

    Returns
    -------
    InjectionTrial
    """
    data = ifu.observe(
        apply_shear(galaxy, g1, g2), line_flux=line_flux, line_wavelength=line_wavelength, rng=rng
    )

    extra_priors = _resolve_free_priors(free_priors, galaxy)
    bad = [k for k in extra_priors if k not in GALAXY_FIELDS]
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f"free_priors may only name DiscGalaxy fields, got {bad}")
    fixed = {f: getattr(galaxy, f) for f in GALAXY_FIELDS if f not in extra_priors}

    if likelihood == "cube":
        lik = IFUCubeLikelihood(
            ifu=ifu,
            line_wavelength=line_wavelength,
            data=data,
            fixed_galaxy_params=fixed,
            fixed_line_flux=line_flux,
        )
    elif likelihood == "moments":
        lik = IFUMomentLikelihood(
            ifu=ifu,
            line_wavelength=line_wavelength,
            data=data,
            fixed_galaxy_params=fixed,
            fixed_line_flux=line_flux,
            snr_threshold=snr_threshold,
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"likelihood must be 'cube' or 'moments', got {likelihood!r}")
    prior = build_prior(
        {
            "g1": (-shear_prior_range, shear_prior_range),
            "g2": (-shear_prior_range, shear_prior_range),
            **extra_priors,
        }
    )
    posterior = fit_shear(prior, lik, n_live=n_live, seed=sampler_seed, n_eff=n_eff)

    summary = posterior.summary()
    g_rec = (summary["g1"][0], summary["g2"][0])
    g_err = tuple(0.5 * (summary[k][1] + summary[k][2]) for k in ("g1", "g2"))
    return InjectionTrial(
        g_true=(float(g1), float(g2)),
        g_rec=g_rec,
        g_err=g_err,
        galaxy=galaxy,
        posterior=posterior if keep_posterior else None,
    )

Trials are ordered shear-major (all galaxies at shears[0], then at shears[1], ...). Trial k always uses the k-th child seed of seed, so results are reproducible; pass the same galaxy list at every shear to compare like with like.

def run_injection(
    galaxies: Sequence[DiscGalaxy],
    shears: Sequence[tuple[float, float]],
    *,
    seed: int,
    verbose: bool = False,
    **recover_kwargs,
) -> list[InjectionTrial]:
    """Run :func:`recover_shear` for every ``(shear, galaxy)`` pair.

    Trials are ordered shear-major (all galaxies at ``shears[0]``, then at
    ``shears[1]``, ...). Trial ``k`` always uses the ``k``-th child seed of
    ``seed``, so results are reproducible; pass the same galaxy list at every
    shear to compare like with like.

    ``recover_kwargs`` are forwarded to :func:`recover_shear` (``ifu``,
    ``line_wavelength`` and ``line_flux`` are required; ``rng`` and
    ``sampler_seed`` are set here and may not be passed).
    """
    if not galaxies or not shears:
        raise ValueError("need at least one galaxy and one shear")
    for reserved in ("rng", "sampler_seed"):
        if reserved in recover_kwargs:
            raise TypeError(f"{reserved!r} is set per-trial from `seed`; do not pass it")

    pairs = [(s, g) for s in shears for g in galaxies]
    seeds = _trial_seeds(seed, len(pairs))
    trials = []
    for k, ((shear, galaxy), (rng, sampler_seed)) in enumerate(zip(pairs, seeds, strict=True)):
        trial = recover_shear(
            galaxy, shear[0], shear[1], rng=rng, sampler_seed=sampler_seed, **recover_kwargs
        )
        trials.append(trial)
        if verbose:
            print(
                f"[{k + 1}/{len(pairs)}] true=({shear[0]:+.3f},{shear[1]:+.3f}) "
                f"rec=({trial.g_rec[0]:+.3f},{trial.g_rec[1]:+.3f}) "
                f"err=({trial.g_err[0]:.3f},{trial.g_err[1]:.3f})"
            )
    return trials

def summarize_trials(trials: Sequence[InjectionTrial]) -> EnsembleSummary:
    """Reduce injection trials to ``(m, c)``, ``sigma_eps``, mean bias and pulls.

    ``mean_bias`` pools all trials regardless of true shear -- meaningful as a
    null test when every trial has ``g_true = 0``, otherwise prefer ``(m, c)``.
    """
    if not trials:
        raise ValueError("need at least one trial")
    true = np.array([t.g_true for t in trials], dtype=float)
    rec = np.array([t.g_rec for t in trials], dtype=float)
    err = np.array([t.g_err for t in trials], dtype=float)
    return EnsembleSummary(
        g1=_summarize_component(true[:, 0], rec[:, 0], err[:, 0]),
        g2=_summarize_component(true[:, 1], rec[:, 1], err[:, 1]),
        n_trials=len(trials),
    )

docs.title: kino.analysis.semester
docs.text:
Batch forecasting across a date range and/or a target list.

kino.analysis.forecast's forecast_ifu/forecast_slit forecast ONE target through ONE night. Real proposal target selection needs the step above that: repeat the same forecast over many nights, to find a semester's best observing windows, and over many candidate targets, to rank them (requested interface, 2026-09-26: "given a telescope/detector, a galaxy spectrum, its RA/Dec, the night and the expected shear, the pipeline returns S/N as a function of seeing... then batch it over a candidate list to find the optimal candidates across a semester"). This module adds exactly that batching layer -- no new physics: it loops forecast_ifu/forecast_slit over dates and targets and collapses each night's full (time, seeing) grid to its single best point.

Real candidate lists are private (CLAUDE.md: never commit one, or use a real target name in code, tests or notebooks); this module and its tests use only synthetic targets.

Cost. A full semester (~180 nights) at a fine seeing/time grid is slow: each night forecast evaluates several times x seeing points, each its own shear_fisher call (a few seconds for an IFU, much slower for a slit -- see kino.analysis.fisher's module docstring). Default to a single representative seeing_ref, a coarse time_step, and a strided date range (:func:semester_dates's step_days) for an exploratory sweep over many candidates; only widen either once a shortlist exists.

def semester_dates(start: str, end: str, step_days: int = 7) -> list[str]:
    """Calendar dates (``YYYY-MM-DD``) from ``start`` to ``end`` inclusive, every ``step_days``.

    A target's visibility changes slowly night to night, so a weekly stride
    (the default) is usually enough to map out a semester's observable
    window without evaluating every single night -- narrow ``step_days``
    once a promising stretch is found.
    """
    if step_days < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"step_days must be >= 1, got {step_days}")
    t0, t1 = Time(start), Time(end)
    if t1 < t0:
        raise ValueError(f"end ({end}) is before start ({start})")
    n_days = int(round((t1 - t0).to_value(u.day)))
    return [(t0 + i * u.day).iso[:10] for i in range(0, n_days + 1, step_days)]

def forecast_over_nights(
    instrument,
    target: ForecastTarget,
    dates: list[str],
    library: SkyLibrary,
    *,
    g: tuple[float, float],
    seeing_ref: u.Quantity,
    site: Site = SOAR,
    solar_flux_fn=None,
    **forecast_kwargs,
) -> NightlyForecast:
    """``target``'s best-case shear forecast on each night in ``dates``.

    Loops ``forecast_ifu``/``forecast_slit`` (auto-selected from
    ``instrument``'s type) over ``dates``, and collapses each night's full
    (time, seeing) grid to its single best point (highest ``shear_snr``).

    Parameters
    ----------
    instrument : IFU or SlitSpectrograph
    dates : list of str
        Calendar dates (``"2027-03-14"``); see :func:`semester_dates` to
        build an evenly-spaced range.
    solar_flux_fn : callable, optional
        ``date -> F10.7`` (s.f.u.). Default:
        ``kino.observing.solar.solar_flux(date)[0]`` (the NOAA-predicted
        monthly mean). A night outside its tabulated months is skipped (left
        NaN) with one warning for the whole run, not an exception, so a long
        date range doesn't abort partway through -- pass your own function
        to cover out-of-table months.
    **forecast_kwargs
        Passed through to ``forecast_ifu``/``forecast_slit`` (``max_airmass``,
        ``time_step``, ``window_kms``, ``include_extinction``,
        ``snr_threshold``, ``priors``, ``estimator``, ``intrinsic_sigma``,
        ``psf_error``).

    Notes
    -----
    A target/instrument mismatch that's independent of the date (the line
    outside the sky library's or the instrument's own wavelength coverage)
    raises on the very first night, exactly as ``forecast_ifu``/
    ``forecast_slit`` already would -- this is a configuration error, not a
    per-night NaN, so it is not caught here (see :func:`rank_candidates` for
    batching over several targets where one bad target shouldn't abort the
    rest).
    """
    forecast_fn = forecast_slit if isinstance(instrument, SlitSpectrograph) else forecast_ifu
    sf_fn = solar_flux_fn or (lambda d: _tabulated_solar_flux(d)[0])
    seeing_ref = u.Quantity(seeing_ref)
    if seeing_ref.isscalar:
        seeing_ref = seeing_ref.reshape(1)

    n = len(dates)
    shear_snr = np.full(n, np.nan)
    shear_snr_stat = np.full(n, np.nan)
    seeing = np.full(n, np.nan) * u.arcsec
    airmass = np.full(n, np.nan)
    time: list[str | None] = [None] * n
    skipped_months: set[str] = set()

    for i, date in enumerate(dates):
        try:
            sf = sf_fn(date)
        except KeyError:
            skipped_months.add(str(date)[:7])
            continue
        night = night_window(site, date)
        fc = forecast_fn(
            instrument, target, night, library, g=g, seeing_ref=seeing_ref,
            solar_flux=sf, site=site, **forecast_kwargs,
        )  # fmt: skip
        if not np.any(np.isfinite(fc.shear_snr)):
            continue
        i_t, j_s = np.unravel_index(np.nanargmax(fc.shear_snr), fc.shear_snr.shape)
        shear_snr[i] = fc.shear_snr[i_t, j_s]
        shear_snr_stat[i] = fc.shear_snr_stat[i_t, j_s]
        seeing[i] = fc.seeing_ref[j_s]
        airmass[i] = fc.airmass[i_t]
        time[i] = fc.times[i_t].iso

    if skipped_months:
        warnings.warn(
            f"no F10.7 prediction for {sorted(skipped_months)}; those nights are NaN "
            "(pass solar_flux_fn to cover them)",
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    return NightlyForecast(
        target=target, dates=list(dates), seeing_ref=seeing_ref, g=g,
        shear_snr=shear_snr, shear_snr_stat=shear_snr_stat, seeing=seeing,
        airmass=airmass, time=time,
    )  # fmt: skip

Unlike :func:forecast_over_nights itself, a target/instrument mismatch here (ValueError from the line falling outside the sky library's or the instrument's wavelength coverage) marks that target undetectable (summary()["detectable"] = False) rather than aborting the whole candidate list -- one bad candidate (e.g. a typo'd redshift) shouldn't block ranking the rest. Returns one :class:NightlyForecast per target, most observable first (summary()["detectable"] = False entries last, in input order).

def rank_candidates(
    instrument,
    targets: list[ForecastTarget],
    dates: list[str],
    library: SkyLibrary,
    *,
    g: tuple[float, float],
    seeing_ref: u.Quantity,
    site: Site = SOAR,
    solar_flux_fn=None,
    **forecast_kwargs,
) -> list[NightlyForecast]:
    """:func:`forecast_over_nights` for every target, ranked by best-night shear S/N.

    Unlike :func:`forecast_over_nights` itself, a target/instrument
    mismatch here (``ValueError`` from the line falling outside the sky
    library's or the instrument's wavelength coverage) marks *that* target
    undetectable (``summary()["detectable"] = False``) rather than aborting
    the whole candidate list -- one bad candidate (e.g. a typo'd redshift)
    shouldn't block ranking the rest. Returns one :class:`NightlyForecast`
    per target, most observable first (``summary()["detectable"] = False``
    entries last, in input order).
    """
    results = []
    for t in targets:
        try:
            results.append(
                forecast_over_nights(
                    instrument,
                    t,
                    dates,
                    library,
                    g=g,
                    seeing_ref=seeing_ref,
                    site=site,
                    solar_flux_fn=solar_flux_fn,
                    **forecast_kwargs,
                )  # fmt: skip
            )
        except ValueError:
            n = len(dates)
            results.append(
                NightlyForecast(
                    target=t,
                    dates=list(dates),
                    seeing_ref=u.Quantity(seeing_ref),
                    g=g,
                    shear_snr=np.full(n, np.nan),
                    shear_snr_stat=np.full(n, np.nan),
                    seeing=np.full(n, np.nan) * u.arcsec,
                    airmass=np.full(n, np.nan),
                    time=[None] * n,
                )  # fmt: skip
            )

    def rank_key(r: NightlyForecast) -> float:
        i = r.best_night_index
        return -r.shear_snr[i] if i is not None else np.inf

    return sorted(results, key=rank_key)

def vlos(self, x, y) -> np.ndarray:
    """Line-of-sight velocity at ``(x, y)``, arcsec -> km/s.

    ``Vlos = v_sys + Vrot(r) * sin(inc) * cos(theta)``, theta measured
    from the major axis in the disc plane (``CLAUDE.md`` convention).
    Positive = redshifted (receding).
    """
    r_disc, cos_theta = self._disc_plane(x, y)
    v_rot = ROTATION_CURVES[self.rotation_curve](r_disc, self.v_flat, self.r_t)
    sin_i = np.sin(np.radians(self.inc))
    return self.v_sys + v_rot * sin_i * cos_theta

def velocity_dispersion(self, x, y) -> np.ndarray:
    """Intrinsic velocity dispersion at ``(x, y)``, arcsec -> km/s."""

    return np.clip(self.sigma0 + self.sigma_grad * r_disc, 0.0, None)

Voxel-level Gaussian log-likelihood of an IFU cube.

log L = -1/2 sum[(d - m)^2 / v + ln v] over every voxel.

Each trial parameter set is forward-modelled through the fixed ifu into the expected cube m (sky + dark baseline included) and compared with the data cube voxel by voxel, with v = m + read noise^2 the expected variance (Poisson source + sky + dark plus read noise, Gaussian-approximated). Nothing is reduced to moments first, so -- unlike :class:IFUMomentLikelihood -- there is no estimator noise bias: on many noise realisations the maximum-likelihood shear was unbiased (to ~1e-4) and its scatter matched the Cramer-Rao bound (:func:kino.analysis.fisher.shear_fisher, estimator="cube") at every S/N tested, from per-spaxel S/N ~ 5 to ~100. It also uses the flux image and the line wings that the moment maps discard.

Parameters are as for :class:IFUMomentLikelihood: g1/g2/line_flux handled here, any other free parameter a DiscGalaxy field.

def summary(self) -> dict[str, tuple[float, float, float]]:
    """``{name: (median, -1sigma, +1sigma)}`` from the 16/50/84th percentiles."""
    out = {}
    for name in self.param_names:
        lo, med, hi = np.percentile(self.samples[name], [16.0, 50.0, 84.0])
        out[name] = (float(med), float(med - lo), float(hi - med))
    return out

def build_prior(free_params: dict) -> Prior:
    """Build a ``nautilus.Prior`` from ``{name: dist}``.

    ``dist`` is either a ``(low, high)`` tuple (uniform) or any object with
    ``.ppf``/``.rvs`` (e.g. a ``scipy.stats`` frozen distribution, or
    :func:`tully_fisher_prior`'s return value) -- exactly what
    ``nautilus.Prior.add_parameter(dist=...)`` accepts.
    """
    prior = Prior()
    for name, dist in free_params.items():
        prior.add_parameter(name, dist=dist)
    return prior

A log-normal scipy.stats distribution for v_flat, centred on the toy Tully-Fisher relation's prediction at flux, with scatter_dex scatter in :math:\log_{10} v_{\rm flat}.

Pass the result as a parameter's dist in :func:build_prior (or directly to nautilus.Prior.add_parameter).

Source code in kino/inference/priors.py 
def tully_fisher_prior(
    flux: float,
    *,
    v0: float,
    flux0: float,
    alpha: float = TOY_TF_ALPHA,
    scatter_dex: float = 0.1,
) -> rv_continuous:
    """A log-normal ``scipy.stats`` distribution for ``v_flat``, centred on
    the toy Tully-Fisher relation's prediction at ``flux``, with
    ``scatter_dex`` scatter in :math:`\\log_{10} v_{\\rm flat}`.

    Pass the result as a parameter's ``dist`` in :func:`build_prior` (or
    directly to ``nautilus.Prior.add_parameter``).
    """
    from scipy.stats import norm

    v_center = tully_fisher_velocity(flux, v0=v0, flux0=flux0, alpha=alpha)
    log_v_center = np.log10(v_center)

    class _LogNormalV(rv_continuous):
        def _ppf(self, q):
            return 10.0 ** norm.ppf(q, loc=log_v_center, scale=scatter_dex)

        def _cdf(self, x):
            with np.errstate(divide="ignore"):
                return norm.cdf(np.log10(x), loc=log_v_center, scale=scatter_dex)

    return _LogNormalV(a=0.0, name="toy_tully_fisher_v_flat")

Normalised (sum=1) 2-D kernel, rasterised at pixel_scale.

wavelength and aperture_diameter set the diffraction scale; obscuration is the fraction of the aperture blocked by a secondary mirror (pass the instrument's own value for consistency with the collecting area used for the photon budget).

def kernel(
    self,
    pixel_scale: u.Quantity,
    wavelength: u.Quantity,
    aperture_diameter: u.Quantity,
    obscuration: float = 0.0,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Normalised (sum=1) 2-D kernel, rasterised at ``pixel_scale``.

    ``wavelength`` and ``aperture_diameter`` set the diffraction scale;
    ``obscuration`` is the fraction of the aperture blocked by a
    secondary mirror (pass the instrument's own value for consistency
    with the collecting area used for the photon budget).
    """
    optical = galsim.OpticalPSF(
        lam=wavelength.to_value(u.nm),
        diam=aperture_diameter.to_value(u.m),
        obscuration=obscuration,
        defocus=self.defocus,
        astig1=self.astig1,
        astig2=self.astig2,
        coma1=self.coma1,
        coma2=self.coma2,
        trefoil1=self.trefoil1,
        trefoil2=self.trefoil2,
        spher=self.spher,
    )
    profile = optical
    if self.seeing_fwhm > 0:
        atmosphere = galsim.Kolmogorov(fwhm=self.seeing_fwhm.to_value(u.arcsec))
        profile = galsim.Convolve([optical, atmosphere])
    image = profile.drawImage(scale=pixel_scale.to_value(u.arcsec))
    kernel = image.array.astype(float)
    return kernel / kernel.sum()

def baseline_electrons(self) -> np.ndarray:
    """Expected sky + dark electrons per channel per spaxel over the whole
    exposure, shape ``(n_wave, 1, 1)`` -- the *known* baseline that
    ``observe`` adds under the line (before noise). Pass it as
    ``subtract_background`` to :func:`kino.analysis.moments.compute_moment_maps`
    to reduce a cube without estimating the background from the data.
    """
    exposure_total = self.exposure_time * self.n_exposures
    sky = np.broadcast_to(
        (self.sky_electron_rate * exposure_total).to_value(u.electron), (self.n_wave,)
    )
    dark = (self.detector.dark_current * exposure_total).to_value(u.electron)
    return (sky + dark)[:, np.newaxis, np.newaxis]

def observe(
    self,
    scene,
    *,
    line_flux: u.Quantity,
    line_wavelength: u.Quantity,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> Datacube:
    """Render ``scene``'s emission line through this IFU.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scene : object
        A :class:`~kino.lensing.scene.LensedScene` (or an unlensed
        ``DiscGalaxy``): must expose ``surface_brightness(x, y)``,
        ``vlos(x, y)``, ``velocity_dispersion(x, y)`` and, on itself or
        a wrapped ``.galaxy``, ``flux`` and ``z``.
    line_flux : Quantity (energy / time / area)
        Intrinsic (unlensed), total flux of the emission line -- see
        the module docstring for how magnification enters.
    line_wavelength : Quantity (wavelength)
        Rest-frame wavelength of the line.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, optional
        ``None`` returns the noiseless expected-count cube; pass a
        seeded generator for one noisy realisation.

    Returns
    -------
    Datacube
        ``flux`` (and ``variance``) in electrons, ``spectral_axis`` in
        wavelength.
    """
    galaxy = getattr(scene, "galaxy", scene)
    z = galaxy.z
    flux_norm = galaxy.flux

    xx, yy, pix_over = self._spatial_grid()
    sb = scene.surface_brightness(xx, yy)
    vlos = scene.vlos(xx, yy) * (u.km / u.s)
    sigma_v = scene.velocity_dispersion(xx, yy) * (u.km / u.s)

    pixel_area_over = pix_over**2
    flux_per_pixel = sb * pixel_area_over.to_value(u.arcsec**2) * (line_flux / flux_norm)

    line_center = doppler_center(vlos, line_wavelength, z)
    sigma_intrinsic = doppler_sigma(sigma_v, line_center)

    wave_edges = np.linspace(self.wavelength_min, self.wavelength_max, self.n_wave + 1)
    wave_centers = 0.5 * (wave_edges[:-1] + wave_edges[1:])
    lsf_sigma = self.lsf.sigma(wave_centers)

    channel_fraction = gaussian_channel_fractions(
        line_center, sigma_intrinsic, lsf_sigma, wave_edges
    )
    flux_cube_over = (
        flux_per_pixel.to_value(line_flux.unit)[np.newaxis, :, :] * channel_fraction
    )

    kernel = self.psf.kernel(
        pix_over,
        wavelength=self.band_center,
        aperture_diameter=self.aperture_diameter,
        obscuration=self.obstruction_fraction,
    )
    flux_cube_over = np.stack(
        [fftconvolve(flux_cube_over[k], kernel, mode="same") for k in range(self.n_wave)]
    )

    ov = _SPATIAL_OVERSAMPLE
    flux_native = flux_cube_over.reshape(self.n_wave, self.ny, ov, self.nx, ov).sum(axis=(2, 4))
    flux_native = flux_native * line_flux.unit

    exposure_total = self.exposure_time * self.n_exposures
    signal_electron = photon_flux_to_electrons(
        flux_native, wave_centers, self.throughput, self.effective_area, exposure_total
    )
    baseline = self.baseline_electrons()

    expected = signal_electron + baseline
    counts, variance = apply_shot_and_read_noise(
        expected, self.detector.read_noise, self.n_exposures, rng
    )

    return Datacube(
        flux=counts,
        spectral_axis=wave_centers,
        spectral_kind="wavelength",
        pixel_scale=self.pixel_scale.to(u.arcsec),
        redshift=z,
        flux_unit=u.electron,
        variance=variance,
        meta={
            "source": "kino.instruments.ifu.IFU.observe",
            "line_wavelength_rest": line_wavelength,
            "line_flux_intrinsic": line_flux,
            "noiseless": rng is None,
        },
    )

    # -- spectrum: truncate to the slit width (fine grid), sum across it,
    # bin down along the slit, crop the margin.
    in_slit = np.abs(v_axis.to_value(u.arcsec)) <= (self.slit_width / 2.0).to_value(u.arcsec)
    spectrum_over_u = flux_cube_over[:, in_slit, :].sum(axis=1)
    spectrum_native_padded = spectrum_over_u.reshape(self.n_wave, n_u_native, ov).sum(axis=2)
    spectrum_native = spectrum_native_padded[:, self.margin : self.margin + self.n_spatial]
    spectrum_native = spectrum_native * line_flux.unit

    signal_electron = photon_flux_to_electrons(
        spectrum_native, wave_centers, self.throughput, self.effective_area, exposure_total
    )
    baseline = self.baseline_electrons()  # (n_wave, 1, 1): sky + dark
    expected_spectrum = signal_electron + baseline[:, 0, :]
    spectrum_counts, spectrum_variance = apply_shot_and_read_noise(
        expected_spectrum, self.detector.read_noise, self.n_exposures, rng
    )

    spectrum = Datacube(
        flux=spectrum_counts[:, :, np.newaxis],
        spectral_axis=wave_centers,
        spectral_kind="wavelength",
        pixel_scale=self.pixel_scale.to(u.arcsec),
        redshift=z,
        flux_unit=u.electron,
        variance=spectrum_variance[:, :, np.newaxis],
        meta={
            "source": "kino.instruments.slit.SlitSpectrograph.observe",
            "line_wavelength_rest": line_wavelength,
            "line_flux_intrinsic": line_flux,
            "slit_width": self.slit_width,
            "slit_pa": self.slit_pa,
            "slit_offset": self.slit_offset,
            "noiseless": rng is None,
        },
    )

    # -- companion broadband image: un-truncated, wavelength-collapsed.
    image_native_percow = flux_cube_over.reshape(
        self.n_wave, n_v_native, ov, n_u_native, ov
    ).sum(axis=(2, 4))
    image_native_percow = image_native_percow * line_flux.unit
    image_signal = photon_flux_to_electrons(
        image_native_percow, wave_centers, self.throughput, self.effective_area, exposure_total
    )
    # `baseline` broadcasts (n_wave, 1, 1) against every image pixel -- correct whether
    # sky_electron_rate is a scalar or, as kino.observing.skymodel's helpers return, a
    # per-channel (n_wave,) array (a bare `* np.ones((n_wave, ny, nx))` here would only
    # broadcast the scalar case; that was this branch's bug until an array-valued rate
    # was first exercised through SlitSpectrograph).

    image_counts, _ = apply_shot_and_read_noise(
        expected_image, self.detector.read_noise, self.n_exposures, rng
    )

    return SlitObservation(
        spectrum=spectrum,
        image=image_counts,
        image_pixel_scale=self.pixel_scale.to(u.arcsec),
        slit_width=self.slit_width,
        slit_length=self.slit_length,
        slit_pa=self.slit_pa,
        slit_offset=self.slit_offset,
    )

def baseline_electrons(self) -> np.ndarray:
    """Expected sky + dark electrons per channel per spaxel over the whole
    exposure, shape ``(n_wave, 1, 1)`` -- the *known* baseline that
    ``observe`` adds under the line (before noise). Pass it as
    ``subtract_background`` to :func:`kino.analysis.moments.compute_moment_maps`

def observe(
    self,
    scene,
    *,
    line_flux: u.Quantity,
    line_wavelength: u.Quantity,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
) -> Datacube:
    """Render ``scene``'s emission line through this IFU.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scene : object
        A :class:`~kino.lensing.scene.LensedScene` (or an unlensed
        ``DiscGalaxy``): must expose ``surface_brightness(x, y)``,
        ``vlos(x, y)``, ``velocity_dispersion(x, y)`` and, on itself or
        a wrapped ``.galaxy``, ``flux`` and ``z``.
    line_flux : Quantity (energy / time / area)
        Intrinsic (unlensed), total flux of the emission line -- see
        the module docstring for how magnification enters.
    line_wavelength : Quantity (wavelength)
        Rest-frame wavelength of the line.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator or None, optional
        ``None`` returns the noiseless expected-count cube; pass a
        seeded generator for one noisy realisation.

    Returns
    -------
    Datacube
        ``flux`` (and ``variance``) in electrons, ``spectral_axis`` in
        wavelength.
    """
    galaxy = getattr(scene, "galaxy", scene)
    z = galaxy.z
    flux_norm = galaxy.flux

    xx, yy, pix_over = self._spatial_grid()
    sb = scene.surface_brightness(xx, yy)
    vlos = scene.vlos(xx, yy) * (u.km / u.s)
    sigma_v = scene.velocity_dispersion(xx, yy) * (u.km / u.s)

    pixel_area_over = pix_over**2
    flux_per_pixel = sb * pixel_area_over.to_value(u.arcsec**2) * (line_flux / flux_norm)

    line_center = doppler_center(vlos, line_wavelength, z)
    sigma_intrinsic = doppler_sigma(sigma_v, line_center)

    wave_edges = np.linspace(self.wavelength_min, self.wavelength_max, self.n_wave + 1)
    wave_centers = 0.5 * (wave_edges[:-1] + wave_edges[1:])
    lsf_sigma = self.lsf.sigma(wave_centers)

    channel_fraction = gaussian_channel_fractions(
        line_center, sigma_intrinsic, lsf_sigma, wave_edges
    )
    flux_cube_over = (
        flux_per_pixel.to_value(line_flux.unit)[np.newaxis, :, :] * channel_fraction
    )

    kernel = self.psf.kernel(
        pix_over,
        wavelength=self.band_center,
        aperture_diameter=self.aperture_diameter,
        obscuration=self.obstruction_fraction,
    )
    flux_cube_over = np.stack(
        [fftconvolve(flux_cube_over[k], kernel, mode="same") for k in range(self.n_wave)]
    )

    ov = _SPATIAL_OVERSAMPLE
    flux_native = flux_cube_over.reshape(self.n_wave, self.ny, ov, self.nx, ov).sum(axis=(2, 4))
    flux_native = flux_native * line_flux.unit

    exposure_total = self.exposure_time * self.n_exposures
    signal_electron = photon_flux_to_electrons(
        flux_native, wave_centers, self.throughput, self.effective_area, exposure_total
    )
    baseline = self.baseline_electrons()

    expected = signal_electron + baseline
    counts, variance = apply_shot_and_read_noise(
        expected, self.detector.read_noise, self.n_exposures, rng
    )

    return Datacube(
        flux=counts,
        spectral_axis=wave_centers,
        spectral_kind="wavelength",
        pixel_scale=self.pixel_scale.to(u.arcsec),
        redshift=z,
        flux_unit=u.electron,
        variance=variance,
        meta={
            "source": "kino.instruments.ifu.IFU.observe",
            "line_wavelength_rest": line_wavelength,
            "line_flux_intrinsic": line_flux,
            "noiseless": rng is None,
        },
    )

docs.title: kino.io.spectrum
docs.text:
1-D galaxy spectra from tables, and emission-line flux measurement.

A forecast needs the galaxy's line flux and redshift. Spectra come from public archives (Legacy Survey/DESI/SDSS, southern surveys, ...) as ASCII or FITS tables in differing conventions, so the reader is deliberately strict about units: a flux column with no unit in the file or in the call raises instead of guessing (SDSS/DESI's 1e-17 erg/s/cm2/A convention is a classic silent factor-of-1e17 error).

Wavelengths are treated as vacuum; SDSS and DESI spectra are vacuum, many other sources quote air wavelengths -- convert first (the ~2 A shift at H-alpha is irrelevant to the line flux but matters for sky-line overlap).

The measured flux is what the spectrograph aperture (a fibre, a slit) collected, not the galaxy's total line flux. Pass aperture_correction when you know the fraction of the galaxy inside that aperture.

Read a spectrum from an ASCII or FITS binary table.

Columns are found by common names (wavelength: wavelength/wave/lam; flux: flux; error: error/err/flux_err or ivar) unless named. loglam (SDSS, log10 of the wavelength in Angstrom) is converted. wavelength_unit and flux_unit are used when the file carries no unit; a missing flux unit raises rather than defaulting.

.fits/.fit files are read with hdu; anything else through astropy.io.ascii (whitespace, CSV, ...; # comment lines are fine). A header-less two- or three-column text file is read as wavelength flux [error].

def read_spectrum(
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    wavelength_col: str | None = None,
    flux_col: str | None = None,
    error_col: str | None = None,
    wavelength_unit: u.UnitBase | str | None = None,
    flux_unit: u.UnitBase | str | None = None,
    hdu: int | str = 1,
    format: str | None = None,  # noqa: A002 -- astropy's own keyword
) -> Spectrum1D:
    """Read a spectrum from an ASCII or FITS binary table.

    Columns are found by common names (wavelength: ``wavelength/wave/lam``;
    flux: ``flux``; error: ``error/err/flux_err`` or ``ivar``) unless named.
    ``loglam`` (SDSS, log10 of the wavelength in Angstrom) is converted.
    ``wavelength_unit`` and ``flux_unit`` are used when the file carries no
    unit; **a missing flux unit raises** rather than defaulting.

    ``.fits``/``.fit`` files are read with ``hdu``; anything else through
    ``astropy.io.ascii`` (whitespace, CSV, ...; ``#`` comment lines are fine).
    A header-less two- or three-column text file is read as
    ``wavelength flux [error]``.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    if path.suffix.lower() in (".fits", ".fit", ".fits.gz"):
        table = Table.read(path, hdu=hdu)
    else:
        table = Table.read(path, format=format or "ascii")
        if all(c.startswith("col") for c in table.colnames):
            table.rename_columns(
                table.colnames, ["wavelength", "flux", "error"][: len(table.colnames)]
            )
    lam_name = _find(table, _WAVE_NAMES, wavelength_col)
    lam_is_log = False
    if lam_name is None and "loglam" in {c.lower() for c in table.colnames}:
        lam_name = next(c for c in table.colnames if c.lower() == "loglam")
        lam_is_log = True
    flux_name = _find(table, _FLUX_NAMES, flux_col)
    if lam_name is None or flux_name is None:
        raise ValueError(f"cannot identify wavelength/flux columns in {table.colnames}")

    lam = np.asarray(table[lam_name], dtype=float)
    if lam_is_log:
        lam, w_unit = 10.0**lam, u.AA
    else:
        w_unit = table[lam_name].unit or (
            None if wavelength_unit is None else u.Unit(wavelength_unit)
        )
        if w_unit is None:
            raise ValueError("wavelength has no unit: pass wavelength_unit (e.g. 'Angstrom')")
    f_unit = table[flux_name].unit or (None if flux_unit is None else u.Unit(flux_unit))
    if f_unit is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "flux has no unit in the file: pass flux_unit explicitly "
            "(e.g. 1e-17 * u.erg / u.s / u.cm**2 / u.AA for SDSS/DESI)"
        )
    if flux_unit is not None and table[flux_name].unit is not None and f_unit != u.Unit(flux_unit):
        raise ValueError(f"file says {f_unit}, call says {flux_unit}: refusing to guess")
    flux = np.asarray(table[flux_name], dtype=float) * f_unit

    err = None
    err_name = _find(table, _ERR_NAMES, error_col)
    if err_name is not None:
        e_unit = table[err_name].unit or f_unit
        err = np.asarray(table[err_name], dtype=float) * e_unit
    elif "ivar" in {c.lower() for c in table.colnames}:
        ivar = np.asarray(
            table[next(c for c in table.colnames if c.lower() == "ivar")], dtype=float
        )
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore"):
            err = np.where(ivar > 0, 1.0 / np.sqrt(ivar), np.inf) * f_unit

    good = np.isfinite(lam) & np.isfinite(flux.value)
    order = np.argsort(lam[good])
    lam_q = (lam[good][order] * w_unit).to(u.AA)
    return Spectrum1D(
        wavelength=lam_q,
        flux=flux[good][order],
        error=None if err is None else err[good][order],
        meta={"source": str(path)},
    )

docs.title: measure_line_flux(spectrum: Spectrum1D, redshift: float, line: str | u.Quantity = 'Halpha', *, half_width: u.Quantity = 1500.0 * u.km / u.s, aperture_correction: float = 1.0) -> LineMeasurement
docs.text:
Integrated flux of one emission line: Gaussian plus linear continuum.

Fits amp * exp(-(lam - mu)^2 / 2 sigma^2) + c0 + c1 (lam - mu) in +/- half_width (velocity) around the expected observed wavelength and integrates the Gaussian: F = amp * sigma * sqrt(2 pi). Uses the spectrum's errors if present, otherwise the scatter of the residuals.

aperture_correction (>= 1) multiplies the flux to estimate the whole galaxy's line flux from what the aperture collected; 1 leaves it as measured. The result is not corrected for Milky Way or internal dust.

Source code in kino/io/spectrum.py 
def measure_line_flux(
    spectrum: Spectrum1D,
    redshift: float,
    line: str | u.Quantity = "Halpha",
    *,
    half_width: u.Quantity = 1500.0 * u.km / u.s,
    aperture_correction: float = 1.0,
) -> LineMeasurement:
    """Integrated flux of one emission line: Gaussian plus linear continuum.

    Fits ``amp * exp(-(lam - mu)^2 / 2 sigma^2) + c0 + c1 (lam - mu)`` in
    ``+/- half_width`` (velocity) around the expected observed wavelength and
    integrates the Gaussian: ``F = amp * sigma * sqrt(2 pi)``. Uses the
    spectrum's errors if present, otherwise the scatter of the residuals.

    ``aperture_correction`` (>= 1) multiplies the flux to estimate the whole
    galaxy's line flux from what the aperture collected; 1 leaves it as
    measured. The result is *not* corrected for Milky Way or internal dust.
    """
    rest = LINES[line] * u.AA if isinstance(line, str) else u.Quantity(line).to(u.AA)
    if aperture_correction < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("aperture_correction must be >= 1")
    expected = rest * (1.0 + redshift)
    dv = (half_width / (C_KMS * u.km / u.s)).decompose().value
    lo, hi = expected * (1 - dv), expected * (1 + dv)
    lam_all = spectrum.wavelength.to_value(u.AA)
    sel = (lam_all >= lo.value) & (lam_all <= hi.value)
    if sel.sum() < 8:
        raise ValueError(
            f"only {int(sel.sum())} spectrum pixels within +/-{half_width} of the expected "
            f"line at {expected:.1f} -- is the line inside the spectrum's coverage?"
        )
    lam = lam_all[sel]
    f_unit = spectrum.flux.unit
    y = spectrum.flux.value[sel]
    sigma_y = None
    if spectrum.error is not None:
        e = spectrum.error.to_value(f_unit)[sel]
        if np.all(np.isfinite(e)) and np.all(e > 0):
            sigma_y = e

    pix = float(np.median(np.diff(lam)))
    sig0 = max(1.0 * pix, expected.value * 100.0 / C_KMS)
    c0 = float(np.median(y))
    amp0 = float(np.max(y) - c0)
    p0 = [amp0, expected.value, sig0, c0, 0.0]
    try:
        popt, pcov = curve_fit(
            _gauss_line, lam, y, p0=p0, sigma=sigma_y, absolute_sigma=sigma_y is not None,
            maxfev=20000,
        )  # fmt: skip
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"line fit did not converge: {exc}") from exc
    amp, mu, sig = popt[0], popt[1], abs(popt[2])
    # with sigma=None curve_fit already scales pcov by the residual variance
    # F = amp * sigma * sqrt(2 pi); propagate including the amp-sigma covariance
    grad = np.array([sig, amp]) * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi)
    cov2 = np.array([[pcov[0, 0], pcov[0, 2]], [pcov[2, 0], pcov[2, 2]]])
    var_f = float(grad @ cov2 @ grad)
    flux = amp * sig * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi) * f_unit * u.AA
    flux_err = np.sqrt(max(var_f, 0.0)) * f_unit * u.AA
    unit = u.erg / u.s / u.cm**2
    f = (flux * aperture_correction).to(unit)
    fe = (flux_err * aperture_correction).to(unit)
    return LineMeasurement(
        flux=f,
        flux_err=fe,
        center=mu * u.AA,
        velocity_offset=(mu - expected.value) / expected.value * C_KMS * u.km / u.s,
        sigma_velocity=sig / mu * C_KMS * u.km / u.s,
        snr=float(abs(f.value) / fe.value) if fe.value > 0 else float("inf"),
    )

docs.title: kino.io.fitsio
docs.text:
FITS read/write for KINO's own mock data products (README.md Phase 4).

Generalizes the ad hoc FITS round-trip that previously lived only inside examples/simulate_one_galaxy.py/run_inference.py into a real, tested kino.io API, used by both those scripts and kino.mocks.catalogue. kino.io.hdf5 mirrors the same four function names for an HDF5-backed alternative.

Datacube layout

write_datacube/read_datacube store a :class:~kino.io.base.Datacube as one extname image extension (default "FLUX") plus, if present, a VARIANCE and a MASK extension (mask as uint8, 1 = masked). Everything needed to reconstruct the spectral axis, pixel scale, redshift, and flux unit is round-tripped through header cards on the data extension itself (BUNIT, SPECKIND, SPECUNIT, SPECVAL0, SPECSTEP, PIXSCALE, REDSHIFT); Datacube.meta (free-form provenance) is JSON-encoded into one METAJSON header card -- astropy's fits.Header folds a long string value across CONTINUE cards automatically, so no manual chunking is needed (verified to round-trip exactly for a representative galaxy-provenance blob).

SlitObservation layout

write_slit_observation/read_slit_observation store the same SPECTRUM/VARIANCE/MASK extensions for obs.spectrum, plus an IMAGE extension for the companion broadband image, with the slit's geometry (obs.slit_width, slit_length, slit_pa, slit_offset, image_pixel_scale) on the IMAGE header (SLITW, SLITLEN, SLITPA, SLITOFFX, SLITOFFY, IMGSCALE; slit_length is derived from n_spatial * pixel_scale on read via :class:~kino.instruments.slit.SlitObservation's own field, so it is written but not required to reconstruct the object).

docs.title: kino.io.kinms
docs.text:
Generate known-truth datacubes with KinMS, for injection-recovery tests.

Thin wrapper around the kinms package (Davis et al. 2013, MNRAS 429, 534; https://github.com/TimothyADavis/KinMSpy) that maps KINO's documented conventions (CLAUDE.md) onto KinMS's cube-generation API and returns a :class:kino.io.base.Datacube. This is Tier A of the validation ladder in TEST_DATA.md: cubes with an exactly known input, used for unit and injection-recovery tests before touching any real or simulated survey data.

Position-angle convention

KinMS's posAng places its disc's redshifted lobe along +y at posAng=0 and rotates it towards -x as posAng increases (verified empirically — KinMS ships no explicit statement of rotation sense). KINO's pa is degrees East of North in the (x=East, y=North) plane, i.e. it rotates from +y towards +x as pa increases. The two rotate in opposite senses, so this wrapper passes posAng=-pa to KinMS to align the kinematic major-axis line with KINO's convention.

The major-axis line is pinned by tests/io/test_kinms.py::test_position_angle_convention. Which end of that line is redshifted is confirmed consistent with kino.galaxy's independently-derived Vlos convention (Phase 1) by tests/galaxy/test_disc.py::test_pa_zero_redshifted_side_matches_kinms_convention and, at the level of a full map rather than two points, by tests/galaxy/test_kinms_consistency.py (Vlos-map correlation > 0.99 against an independently generated KinMS cube).
